messages:
Samira K: quick proposal — extract probe normalization + hint generation out of the runtime into a standalone 'policy-preprocessor' service. idea is to keep runtime minimal and let console/sim reuse the same logic. opt-in to start. thoughts?

Ajay P: extra network hop worries me. runtime currently normalizes raw probes inline; adding a service could add latency and failure modes. what are our SLO targets here?

Kevin L: agreed latency is the main risk, but if preprocessor returns compact 'hints' with TTL we can short-circuit heavy compute in runtime. example response shape below (simplified):
```json
{
  "hints": [
    {"route_id": "r-123", "penalty_hint": 0.12, "ttl_s": 30},
    {"route_id": "r-456", "penalty_hint": 0.64, "ttl_s": 10}
  ],
  "version": "v1"
}
```

Samira K: exactly. other wins: versioned outputs, centralizing complex normalization heuristics, reuse by simulator and console for explainability. reduces duplication.

Marta S: cache invalidation and geo-staleness are tricky. preprocessor must emit per-region stamps and sequence numbers so runtime can prefer local hints when stale. also TTLs must be conservative for cross-region traffic.

Ajay P: fallback strategy is essential. runtime must handle missing or expired hints by computing locally (same codepath as today). so keep the local compute as a fallback to preserve safety.

Kevin L: telemetry requirements: track preproc_call_latency_p50/95/99, preproc_hint_miss_rate (fraction of requests that fell back). add a histogram of hint_ttl_remaining at use time. those will prove benefit.

policy-bot: RFC checklist: link=https://rfd.internal/policy-preprocessor, required_fields=[interface, sloa, auth, rollout]. Please attach a short API schema and perf targets.

Samira K: rollout suggestion: feature-flagged opt-in per-tenant -> canary in us-west (10% traffic) for 2 weeks, compare runtime CPU per-token and hint_miss_rate. If stable, expand by region.

Marta S: ops notes — circuit breaker + fast-fail semantics (500/timeout => runtime fallback). instrumentation for preprocessor health (up/down counts). security — preprocessor must accept only tenant_id and probe aggregates; do NOT accept user PII. tie to our KMS for signing responses if we worry about spoofing.

Ajay P: interface sketch: POST /v1/preprocessor?tenant_id={t} body: { probes: [{route, latency_ms, success_rate}], sample_size }. reply: { hints: [{route, penalty_hint, ttl_s}], version }. on missing hints runtime uses local compute. sample curl:
```bash
curl -X POST "https://preproc.internal/v1/preprocessor?tenant_id=acme" \\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \\n  -d '{"probes": [{"route":"r-123","latency_ms":120,"p99":250}], "sample_size": 1200}'
```

Kevin L: rough perf estimate: preprocessor adds ~2–6ms network + ~0.5–1ms compute for hints vs current in-runtime compute ~6–12ms in worst-case. net win at high QPS and when hints hit. but we must bench on realistic probe shapes. also watch variance — tail latency could bite.

Samira K: action items: (1) Samira -> PoC preproc service + spec doc, (2) Ajay -> add runtime fallback path + unit tests, (3) Marta -> spec auth + SLOs + ops runbook, (4) Kevin -> telemetry dashboard mocks. check-in next Tue.

Marta S: +1 on runbook. add required k8s resource limits for preproc (CPU burst profiles) and a chaos test for timeouts.

Ajay P: will add a toggle to runtime config: preproc.enabled and preproc.timeout_ms (default 30ms). fallback path will increment metric preproc_local_compute_count.

Kevin L: I'll draft the dashboard: preproc_rt_p95, hint_miss_rate, percent_token_cpu_saved, fallback_rate. quick experiments could use traffic shadowing first.

Samira K: ok thanks all. if nobody objects I'll open the RFC PR by EOD and attach a minimal API schema + rollout checklist. :rocket:
